**What I found**
The gate is not doing its job. In `eslint.config.mjs`, the second block (`files: ['**/*.js']`, lines 15–26) sets `no-restricted-syntax` again with only the `DebuggerStatement` selector. In ESLint flat config, a later block that sets the same rule replaces its options. It does not add to them. So every file under `src/` ends up with only the debugger check, and the auth-internals selector (line 9) never runs anywhere. That is why `src/billing/invoice.js:1` (`import { signToken } from '../auth/internal/token.js'`) passes. The green history proves nothing, because this rule has never been seen to fail. The fix is to make the rule check again and add a CI test that proves it does (the record calls this RESTORE, plus a PROVE guard).

**Why it matters**
If nothing changes, any module can keep importing auth internals and `npm run lint` will stay green. Once you fix the config, lint goes red on `invoice.js` immediately. `src/auth/index.js` has no public way to get `signToken`, so that violation needs a decision before the fix can merge.

**Do this first**
1. In `eslint.config.mjs`, change the second block's `no-restricted-syntax` entry to `'no-debugger': 'error'`. That way the two blocks no longer set the same rule.
2. Add this CI step as the test that proves the gate works. It must exit 1 and print the auth message:
   `echo "import { signToken } from '../auth/internal/token.js';" | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename src/billing/__control__.js`
   It goes through the full config, so if a later block hides the rule again, this step fails.
3. Clear the existing violation before or in the same PR. Either the auth owner adds a public export in `src/auth/index.js` (for example, an invoice-link token function) and `invoice.js` imports that, or `invoice.js` goes on a named, owned exception list that is only allowed to shrink. The first is better because it is a single violation.

**What I did not check**
- I didn't run lint or the control because I have no shell in this session. Run `npm run lint` before and after the change, then run the stdin command above.
- I didn't search for other imports of auth internals that are hiding behind the same shadowing. Search with `rg "auth.internal" src --glob '!src/auth/**'`.
- The CI wiring and the claim that lint blocks merge come from your description. This directory isn't a git repo and has no pipeline files, so I couldn't confirm either.
